result.summary: Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md + docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md exactly as designed, with two flagged deviations (see issues). Schema (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts): relaxed NOT NULL on profiles.first_name/last_name/company/position/is_student/experience_level; added phone_skipped/email_skipped/links_github_skipped/links_linkedin_skipped/links_site_skipped (boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false). Migration generated via `drizzle-kit generate` in apps/bot (never hand-written) -- apps/bot/drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql contains exactly the 11 ALTER TABLE statements the schema doc's own §5 predicted (6 DROP NOT NULL + 5 ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT false), confirmed by direct comparison. New apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts: REQUIRED_PROFILE_FIELDS/OPTIONAL_PROFILE_FIELDS (§2.1's fixed order), getProfileByUserId, determineNextProfileField/isProfileComplete (§2.2's exact 3-step derivation table, pure, no I/O beyond the already-fetched record), isNonBlank/isValidEmailFormat/isValidStudentAnswer/isValidExperienceLevelAnswer (§2.3), writeRequiredProfileField/writeOptionalProfileField/markOptionalProfileFieldSkipped (§2.4's insert-if-absent/update-one-column upserts on profiles_user_id_unique, un-skipping on answer), parseProfileEditFields/validateProfileEditInput (§4.2, moved here per the design's own note), formatProfileDump (§2.5 -- S11 redaction does NOT apply here per the design's own stated exception: a direct reply to the profile's own owner). New apps/bot/src/domain/onboarding.ts: determineOnboardingStep (§3.1's exact 4-branch table) and advanceOnboarding (§3.2) -- the one function every entry point calls; never reads/writes profiles while !hasConsented. New apps/bot/src/handlers/profile.ts: sendProfileFieldPrompt (§4.4's 11 per-field prompt builders, including the phone step's reply-keyboard Skip button forced by request_contact's KeyboardButton-only constraint, §8.4), makeProfileCommandHandler/makeProfileEditHandler/makeProfileChapterHandler+its callback (§4.1-4.3), makeProfileTextAnswerHandler/makeProfileContactHandler (§4.5 -- state derived FRESH from the DB on every message, nothing held in process memory, the exact property AC1 tests), makeProfileSkipCallbackHandler/makeProfileStudentCallbackHandler/makeProfileExperienceCallbackHandler (§4.6's derive-then-gate discipline implemented literally in the same 7-step order the design states, comments citing each step number). Modified apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts: buildConsentKeyboard/CONSENT_AGREE_CALLBACK_PATTERN/matchText/assignChapterOrPrompt changed from file-private to exported per §3.3; all three existing greeting tail-points (makeStartHandler, makeChapterCallbackHandler, makeConsentCallbackHandler's non-deep-link branch) now call advanceOnboarding before falling back to the plain greeting, unchanged for anyone already 'ready'. Modified apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts: new profile.* catalog block (38 keys), placeholder copy per decisions/0002. Modified apps/bot/src/index.ts: registers /profile, /profile_edit, /profile_chapter, the profile:chapter/skip/student/experience callback patterns, and the two generic message:text/message:contact listeners. New unit tests: apps/bot/src/domain/profile.test.ts (18 cases -- determineNextProfileField's full derivation table including AC1's own 3-answered-then-4th-next shape and AC2's all-skipped-completes shape, isValidEmailFormat's AC6 boundary table, parseProfileEditFields/validateProfileEditInput including the all-or-nothing invalid-label collection and the 'skip' token bypassing format validation) and apps/bot/src/domain/onboarding.test.ts (4 cases -- the full determineOnboardingStep branch table, including AC3's own mechanism: consent-needed wins regardless of chapter/profile state). AC verification -- all 6 verified live against a real scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432; migrated with `drizzle-kit migrate`; a real grammy.Bot with a dummy token + manually-supplied botInfo, bot.api.config.use() intercepting outbound calls, bot.handleUpdate() dispatching synthetic Update objects through the real handlers -- the established pattern from REQ-013 through REQ-018's own test specs, e.g. docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-018.md's harness note). AC1 (restart mid-form resumes correctly, first 3 stored): ran the harness as one `npx tsx` process (PID confirmed distinct from the second) answering /start, consent, and the first 3 required fields (firstName/lastName/company) for tg_id 1000000201; that process then exited via its own `process.exit(0)`. Queried Postgres directly BETWEEN the two halves: `SELECT first_name,last_name,company,position FROM profiles...` returned exactly ('First','Last','Acme Inc', NULL) -- proving the row is a legal persisted mid-form state, not merely in-memory. Started a genuinely SEPARATE `npx tsx` invocation (new OS process, no shared memory with the first) that sent only the 4th answer ('Engineer'); it correctly resumed at the 5th field (isStudent -- sent the Yes/No inline keyboard), and a follow-up SELECT confirmed all 4 fields now persisted. This is real process-kill-and-restart evidence, not a same-process re-run. AC2 (skip every optional field still completes): dispatched a full run answering all 6 required fields then skipping all 5 optional fields (phone via the reply-keyboard Skip button text match, the other 4 via their inline profile:skip: callbacks) for tg_id 1000000202; the flow ended with profile.completedNotice ('Your profile is complete...'), and a direct SELECT confirmed all 5 value columns NULL and all 5 *_skipped flags true. AC3 (declining consent leaves zero profiles rows, blocks plainly): for tg_id 1000000203, ran /start (consent prompt shown), then sent a forged plain-text answer ('SomeName' -- no-op, determineOnboardingStep correctly derives consent-needed regardless of the text listener's own field logic) and a forged profile:skip:phone callback (no-op, re-shows the identical consent prompt) -- confirmed live: SELECT count(*) FROM profiles for this user = 0, users.consent_pd_at still NULL, and the process completed with no exception (captured output is exactly two consent-prompt sendMessage calls, never an error). AC4 (already-complete profile asked no question on 2nd pass -- design §8.3's own named interim substitute, since REQ-020 doesn't exist yet): completed a full profile for tg_id 1000000204 via advanceOnboarding/the guided flow, cleared the captured-calls buffer, then dispatched /profile again -- captured exactly 2 sendMessage calls (the formatProfileDump view + the editHint line), zero of the 11 field prompts. AC5 (phone+email entered, error path logs/payload contain neither value): for tg_id 1000000205, entered a real-looking phone number as free text (accepted, stored) then an invalid email string ('not-an-email') at the email step -- captured the rejection reply (profile.invalidEmailFormat, no echo of the value) and grepped the full captured-calls JSON plus process stderr for both the literal phone digits and the literal rejected email string: zero matches in either. Also grepped apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts, domain/onboarding.ts, and handlers/profile.ts for any log.* call: zero matches -- this requirement's own code never logs at all, so S11 is satisfied both structurally (no log call exists to leak through) and by direct negative-case verification. DB check confirmed the phone was legitimately stored (the user's own data, not a log) while the rejected email was never written (email NULL, email_skipped false). AC6 (email accepted absent, format-validated only if supplied): AC6a -- tg_id 1000000206 skipped email via the inline Skip button; DB shows email NULL, email_skipped true, flow proceeded to the next field with no format check ever invoked (isValidEmailFormat is only called from the free-text branch, never the skip branch, confirmed by code inspection matching the live behavior). AC6b -- tg_id 1000000207 skipped every earlier optional field then typed a valid 'ada@example.com' at the email step; DB shows the email stored verbatim, email_skipped false, flow proceeded. Both branches exercised live. Harness script apps/bot/scratch-verify-req019.ts was written, run for all 6 ACs (7 dispatch scenarios), then deleted; `docker compose down -v` torn down the scratch Postgres; `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean (no stray files) before writing this handoff. Commands run from repo root, exit 0 each, real output: `npm run build` (both workspaces -- Next.js build succeeded, `tsc -p apps/bot/tsconfig.json` clean, zero errors); `npm run lint` (0 errors; 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings, unrelated to this diff, unchanged from before); `npx vitest run` (12 files / 142 tests passed -- up from the pre-existing 10 files / 118 tests, net +2 files / +24 tests, all in the two new profile.test.ts/onboarding.test.ts files, zero regressions in any of the other 10 existing files).

npm run build (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces, tsc clean
npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web warnings)

docker compose (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml) up -d; pg_isready polled to ready; npx drizzle-kit migrate applied cleanly; \d profiles confirmed the exact 23-column shape the schema doc specifies
npx tsx scratch-verify-req019.ts <case> for ac1a, ac1b (separate OS process), ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5, ac6a, ac6b -- all captured outputs and DB SELECTs quoted in result.summary
grep -rn "log\.\(info\|warn\|error\|debug\)" apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts apps/bot/src/domain/onboarding.ts apps/bot/src/handlers/profile.ts -> no matches (AC5/S11)
grep -n "15551234567" / "not-an-email" across ac5's captured JSON + stderr -> no matches in either (AC5)

ac_results.AC1: PASS -- real process kill-and-restart (two separate npx tsx invocations) resumes at the 4th required field with the first 3 persisted, confirmed by direct SQL between and after both halves
ac_results.AC2: PASS -- skipping every optional field (mixed reply-keyboard text match for phone, inline callbacks for the other four) still reaches completedNotice; DB confirms all 5 *_skipped flags true, all 5 value columns NULL
ac_results.AC3: PASS -- zero profiles rows, consent_pd_at still NULL, a forged plain-text answer and a forged skip callback both no-op and re-show the plain consent prompt, no exception
ac_results.AC4: PASS -- second /profile for an already-complete profile sends exactly the view dump + edit hint, zero field prompts (design §8.3's own named interim substitute, since REQ-020 does not exist yet)
ac_results.AC5: PASS -- neither the entered phone nor the rejected email string appears anywhere in captured API output or stderr; zero log.* calls exist anywhere in this requirement's new code
ac_results.AC6: PASS -- email skip (AC6a) never invokes format validation (email NULL, skipped=true); a valid typed email (AC6b) is accepted and stored verbatim

issues.description: domain/onboarding.ts imports `Context` from grammy and calls `ctx.reply`, in tension with decisions/0004-telegram-framework-grammy.md's consequence that 'domain logic ... goes in framework-free modules that handlers call, never inside handler bodies.' This is exactly what docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md §3.2 specifies (advanceOnboarding(ctx: Context, ...) sending the next prompt as its one side effect, reasoned there as mirroring handlers/start.ts's own assignChapterOrPrompt convention) and that design already passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR twice (handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-01b-design-validator-regate.json). Implemented exactly as designed per this run's own instruction to implement the design rather than resolve conflicts unilaterally; flagged here per core-directives.md's 'a decisions/ record is never overridden by anything above it... stop and flag it for REVIEWER sign-off' rule rather than silently reconciled in either direction. No other domain/*.ts file in this codebase imports grammy.

The design's own advanceOnboarding signature (REQ-019.md §3.2) is stated as returning Promise<"prompted" | "ready">, but §3.2 step 4's own prose requires the CALLER to run assignChapterOrPrompt on a chapter-needed outcome and call advanceOnboarding again -- a third outcome the stated 2-value return type has no room for. This implementation's advanceOnboarding returns "chapter-needed" as a third literal so handlers/profile.ts (which, unlike handlers/start.ts's three call sites, has no pre-existing chapter gate of its own) can actually implement step 4 as written for a brand-new user running /profile before ever running /start -- the exact case §4.1 itself says this design exists to cover ('a bare /profile from a brand-new user ... still gets the correct next question rather than a dead end'). A second, related gap resolved pragmatically rather than by invented business rule: the design's hasChapter boolean does not by itself terminate for the pre-existing zero-active-chapters edge case (REQ-014's noActiveChapters branch, where chapterId legitimately stays NULL forever) -- this implementation's reachReadyOrPrompt helper (handlers/profile.ts) mirrors handlers/start.ts's own established precedent of proceeding unconditionally once assignChapterOrPrompt resolves to "continue", rather than re-deriving hasChapter and risking an infinite chapter-needed loop for that edge case. Both choices are documented inline at the helper's definition. Not exercised by any of REQ-019's own 6 ACs (none involve a zero-active-chapters chapter or a bare /profile before /start), so no live evidence was captured for this specific path beyond the code-level reasoning; flagging for REVIEWER/TEST-DESIGNER awareness rather than silently declaring it out of scope.
